newsitem.title: UK: GUS sees no quick fix for home shopping.
newsitem.headline: GUS sees no quick fix for home shopping.

text.p: UK home-shopping group Great Universal Stores Plc on Thursday said shifting its mail order business towards high growth direct mail and away from the declining agency market would be a gradual process.

GUS chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale told a news conference the group was testing out four direct mail catalogues this year -- one selling Disney products, a Thomas Burberry catalogue, a specialised sportswear catalogue and Style Plus for larger size clothes.
"The likelihood is we will look at the outturn this autumn then decide where we go from here," he said.
Wolfson said agency mail order business, where agents get commission for securing orders, was still viable, but this sector of the market was in long term decline.

The bulk of GUS's home shopping is via "big book" catalogues selling a vast range of merchandise, but the growth in home shopping has shifted to smaller more upmarket niche catalogues which have proliferated in the United States.
GUS's competitors, including Marks and Spencer Plc and Burton Group Plc, are already moving into the direct mail market.
Wolfson said GUS had the advantage of having a ready made infrastructure for mail order, but was now looking for a product that would appeal to the middle market.
"Purchasing power is going to the middle market. You have to have an offer to appeal to the middle market," he said.
GUS earlier announced a two percent drop in annual profits to 549.1 million stg, and a fall in operating profits from home shopping to 157.6 million stg from 187.4 million.
He said the group had no plans for major acquisitions or other corporate activity after buying U.S. credit information group Experian for $1.7 billion last year.

Wolfson noted suggestions that GUS should spin off its Burberry classic clothing business, but said a year when it had reported flat profits was probably not the time to do it. Burberry's operating profits slipped to 61.7 million stg from 62.8 million.

He said he was not particularly wedded to the current shape of the group, which he described as a conglomerate of six separate businesses, including retailing, financial services and information services. But it was not easy to change things quickly.
"The shape of the group is not easy to change overnight," he said.
